title: Essential surjectivity of the enriched localization unit
statement: Use small simplicial categories, the Bergner model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$, and derived-pushout localization $q:C\to L_WC$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Here $W$ is any set of vertex arrows; $\pi_0$ has the same objects and path components of mapping simplicial sets as morphisms. All displayed categories fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. For every small simplicial category $C$ and every set $W$ of its vertex arrows, $\pi_0q:\pi_0C\to\pi_0L_WC$ is essentially surjective: every object of $L_WC$ is isomorphic in $\pi_0L_WC$ to $q(c)$ for some object $c$ of $C$. No fibrancy, cofibrancy or saturation hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-arrow-attachment-localization]. Choose its factorization $[1]\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{r}\mathbb J$ with $i$ a cofibration and $r$ a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, and form $\Gamma=C\amalg_{\coprod_W[1]}\coprod_W K$, with canonical map $j:C\to\Gamma$. The cited statement gives an isomorphism $e:\Gamma\cong L_WC$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ under $C$, so $e\circ j=q$ there. This assertion applies to arbitrary small $C$ and arbitrary labelled vertex arrows; it does not require $C$ to be cofibrant or fibrant.

source.place: HTT Notation A.3.5.1 and Remark A.3.5.2 (printed pp.891--892), interval-attachment construction, with Proposition A.3.5.5 (printed p.893), its homotopy mapping characterization; agent object-set and endpoint argument. Online source read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-category-degreewise-colimits] to the small pushout diagram of Step 1. Its object-set clause identifies $\operatorname{Ob}\Gamma$ with $\operatorname{Ob}C\amalg_{\coprod_W\{0,1\}}\coprod_W\operatorname{Ob}K$. This set pushout is the disjoint union modulo the endpoint identifications. Thus every object of $\Gamma$ is represented either by $c\in\operatorname{Ob}C$ or by an object $x$ in a labelled copy of $K$. This calculation permits repeated endpoints and loops in $W$.

proof.text: For an object $x$ of an attached copy of $K$, use the factorization in [lem-coef-simplicial-arrow-attachment-localization] and the Dwyer--Kan definition in [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. The functor $\pi_0r:\pi_0K\to\pi_0\mathbb J$ is an equivalence, hence fully faithful. The unique arrows $r(x)\to0$ and $0\to r(x)$ in $\pi_0\mathbb J$ lift to arrows between $x$ and $i(0)$ in $\pi_0K$. Faithfulness and the identity compositions in $\mathbb J$ show that these lifts are inverse. Apply the functor from this copy of $K$ to $\Gamma$: the resulting isomorphism identifies the image of $x$ with the image of $i(0)$, which the pushout relation identifies with $j(\operatorname{source}w)$. Objects represented by $c\in C$ are already $j(c)$. Therefore every object of $\pi_0\Gamma$ is isomorphic to some $j(c)$.

proof.text: Use the induced path-component functors up to natural isomorphism from [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. Dwyer--Kan replacements induce equivalences on path-component categories, so the isomorphism $e$ of Step 1 induces an equivalence $E:\pi_0\Gamma\simeq\pi_0L_WC$. Since that isomorphism is under $C$, there is a natural isomorphism $E\circ\pi_0j\cong\pi_0q$. For $y\in\operatorname{Ob}L_WC$, choose $x\in\operatorname{Ob}\Gamma$ and an isomorphism $y\cong E(x)$ by essential surjectivity of $E$. Step 3 supplies $c\in C$ and $x\cong j(c)$. Applying $E$ and composing with the displayed natural isomorphism gives $y\cong E(x)\cong E(j(c))\cong q(c)$. This proves the assertion for the chosen representative of the derived localization as well as for the strict attachment model.
